images.title: Putting in a zero pair
images.purpose: Show that a zero pair can be put in so 6 positive tokens can be taken away from 5, leaving 1 negative token.
images.composition: Two token rows stacked with wide space between them, equation centred below.
images.exact_structure: Top row: 6 positive tokens in teal #0072B2 in a line, then 1 negative token in amber #E69F00 directly after them; the 6th teal token and the amber token are enclosed together in one reddish purple #CC79A7 rounded outline. Bottom row: exactly 1 amber negative token alone. Exactly 7 tokens in the top row, 1 in the bottom row, 1 outline.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
more than one zero pair outlined
images.takeaway: A zero pair keeps the value the same, so you can take away 6 from 5 and be left with −1.
images.description: Top row of 6 teal positive tokens and 1 amber negative token, with the last teal and the amber circled as a zero pair; below, 1 amber token is left, so (+5) − (+6) = −1.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the circled pair and say why it is worth zero, then at the single token left.

image_decisions.why: Showing the zero pair and what is left is a picture idea; one clean image carries it.
